transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Bluehaven - Head of ML); Priya Sharma (Bluehaven - Eng Mgr); Daniel Wu (Bluehaven - SRE)

Summary:
Light POC weekly sync focused on TTFT (first token), streaming pathing and kernel choice. SE ran microbenchmarks last week; results showed mixed wins depending on sequence length and quantization. Decision needed: two candidate kernel stacks for final pilot run and whether to use streaming-first or batch-first streaming.

Topics: TTFT numbers, streaming chunking, sequence length distribution, kernel A vs kernel B (cu-optimized vs custom fused kernels), quantization impact, dedicated vs hosted pilot economics, VPC peering for live benchmarks, next steps. 

Action items (high level): listed below.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): okay hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday, uh we'll try to keep this to an hour..
[00:12] Liam (Bluehaven): yep thanks, got Priya and Daniel here, quick heads up we've got some meetings but we'll stay for the deep part.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): quick recap - I ran the kernel A/B microbench on the redwood-v1-quant sample set, across 64, 128, 256 seq lengths. results were.. um interesting, so at seq=64 kernel A (cu-optimized) is around 72ms TTFT median, kernel B (fused custom) 68ms but CPU overhead higher on preproc. at seq=256 kernel B wins by a larger margin, like 90ms vs 115ms.
[01:03] Priya (Bluehaven): wait can you repeat the 256 numbers, we care about the tail and the 95th.
[01:09] Carlos: sure, so median 90ms, 95th about 160ms for kernel B; kernel A median 115ms, 95th 210ms. caveat: kernel B uses a custom GEMM path that improves attention for longer sequences but increases memory pressure so KV cache thrashing for very high concurrency.
[01:40] Liam: okay that's promising for our long customer sessions but our typical session is short - median 40 tokens, 99th is around 220 tokens.
[01:52] Maya: that's helpful - so we need to weigh median TTFT vs 95/99 for our workload. also streaming: Carlos, you had a test toggling early-token streaming on? what was effect on TTFT?
[02:05] Carlos: yeah, with streaming enabled and a 32-token chunk stream window the observed first-byte latency was slightly worse, like +8-12ms, but user perceived TTFT improved because tokens start returning earlier during generation; so for UI the perceived latency is better even if first-byte micro is up. there's also more CPU overhead due to chunking.
[02:35] Priya: hm our UX team prioritizes perceived latency, but engineering warns about CPU cost. we have a strict budget.
[02:43] Daniel: infrastructure note - if we go with kernel B's memory pattern, we might need extra GPU memory reservation or pin a larger instance. can you quantify?
[02:52] Carlos: rough ballpark, kernel B increases peak VRAM by about 5-10% for our 2.7B-ish model; with heavy KV cache use we saw OOMs at high concurrency unless we reduce batch size.
[03:08] Liam: does Redwood have a graceful fallback? like route to smaller quantized variant if memory pressure spikes?
[03:15] Maya: yes we can set routing policy - fallback to redwood-v1-small-quant with identical API, and we can do canary rollouts for a portion of traffic. we should define the thresholds.
[03:30] Priya: security check - we need to run benchmarks within our VPC, we can't allow raw sample traces to leave. SSO and KMS integration are blockers for private pilot.
[03:40] Maya: understoood; we've done VPC peering for other customers, and KMS/HSM can be integrated for Private. i'll send the security doc.
[03:48] Daniel: do you support customer-managed KMS or only Redwood-managed?
[03:52] Carlos: we support both on Private; for Dedicated we can bring your KMS with an HSM connector; hosted only Redwood-managed KMS but with envelope encryption.
[04:03] Liam: pricing - dedicated pilot economics? are we locked into monthly minimums?
[04:07] Maya: for pilot we have a time-boxed dedicated pilot (2-4 weeks) with prorated commit and a burst buffer option; i'll send a pricing note after this call.
[04:18] Priya: good. also one more thing - can we run the deep kernel run during our low traffic window? midnight at PST is best for us.
[04:26] Carlos: yes we can schedule a 2 hour run during your midnight window. need network/peering and logs.
[04:33] Liam: one more tech question - sequence length histogram we gave last week was sample biased; we'll upload full 30-day histogram.
[04:40] Maya: perfect, that will help optimizer suggestions for batching and caching.
[04:46] Carlos: quick note - when we tested quantization (8-bit symmetric vs 4-bit GPTQ style), 4-bit gave ~1.6x speedup but with slightly degraded quality on our eval prompts. there's a tradeoff.
[05:00] Priya: can you share the eval prompt set and delta metrics?
[05:03] Carlos: yes, i'll upload a CSV with Rouge/BLEU-adj metrics and human eval notes.
[05:09] Daniel: for the benchmarks can Redwood instrument per-token timing and token-level traces? we need enough telemetry to tie to infra.
[05:15] Carlos: yes, we can produce per-token timing with our tracing hooks, though sample rate might be limited for production runs.
[05:22] Liam: are there any known regressions with mps/amd cards? we use nvidia but curious.
[05:28] Carlos: current kernels are heavily optimized for NVIDIA CUDA; we do have experimental ROCm paths but performance varies, i wouldn't run the A/B there.
[05:35] Priya: okay, what's the proposal for the kernel decision?
[05:38] Maya: SE proposes two candidate stacks: A) cu-optimized standard kernels - lower memory, simpler ops, better tail in some cases; B) fused custom kernels - better mid/long sequence median but needs more memory and has higher preproc CPU. Run 2 hour A/B on your traffic slice, gather 95/99th, and then choose.
[06:00] Liam: that makes sense. can we also include a streaming-first config vs batch-first config in the same run?
[06:06] Carlos: yes we can toggle streaming chunk size and measure perceived latency vs resource usage across both kernels.
[06:12] Priya: timeline?
[06:15] Maya: propose milestones: customer uploads logs by Tues (2026-06-29), SE runs benchmarks Wed-Thu (2026-06-30 to 07-01) overnight, SE shares results by Fri (2026-07-02), then decision and pilot pricing finalized next week.
[56:58] Maya: recap - action items: Carlos runs kernel A/B + quant profiles; Maya sends dedicated pilot pricing & security doc; Bluehaven provides full histogram and opens peering; schedule 2 hour run at midnight PST; share results.
[57:05] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the data-driven approach.
[57:10] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs. bye.

End of transcript.
